name: Semantic authority preservation
canonicalCondition: HDIP-CLA SHALL NOT incompatibly redefine concepts, relationships or invariants owned by GEDRM, GEARM, GEAIRM or other applicable semantic authorities.

name: Product authority preservation
canonicalCondition: Generic Product identity, Product Intrinsic Nature and Product qualification SHALL remain governed by BPS/PIN rather than inferred by HDIP.

name: Product-family authority preservation
canonicalCondition: Data Product, Information Product, AI Product and other Product-family qualification/classification SHALL remain with the applicable Product-family authority.

name: Scoped authority
canonicalCondition: Authority used by HDIP SHALL be explicit for an applicable scope, role, purpose, lifecycle state and/or jurisdiction where those distinctions matter; platform participation SHALL NOT imply universal authority.

name: Shared-realization non-transfer
canonicalCondition: Co-location, shared storage, shared runtime, shared registry, shared UI or shared platform realization SHALL NOT by itself transfer semantic, Product, policy, decision or ownership authority.

name: Semantic-gap escalation
canonicalCondition: Where HDIP needs a semantic concept not owned by HDIP, the gap SHALL be referred to or extended through the appropriate semantic authority rather than silently minted as platform semantics.

name: Authority non-transitivity
canonicalCondition: Authority, approval, entitlement, policy applicability or ownership SHALL NOT become automatically transitive merely because a dependency, composition or interaction crosses an HDIP boundary.

name: Responsibility before component
canonicalCondition: A canonical HDIP ABB or mandatory implementation responsibility SHALL be justified by explicit architectural responsibility; a noun, tool, service label or historical box alone is insufficient.

name: Logical plane semantics
canonicalCondition: A future HDIP Plane SHALL represent a coherent logical responsibility grouping and SHALL NOT imply a mandatory system, deployment unit, network tier, team, organizational boundary or lifecycle step.

name: Topology independence
canonicalCondition: HDIP-CLA conformance SHALL NOT depend on centralized, federated, distributed, edge, embedded, provider-managed or hybrid deployment topology unless a narrower Profile explicitly requires it.

name: Many-to-many realization
canonicalCondition: One implementation MAY realize responsibilities from several HDIP logical structures, and one HDIP responsibility MAY be distributed across several implementations.

name: Source-plane non-equivalence
canonicalCondition: GEDRA, GEARA and GEAIRA plane numbering, placement or lexical similarity SHALL NOT force one-to-one HDIP plane mapping.

name: Cross-cutting visibility
canonicalCondition: A responsibility that is cross-cutting in an applicable source architecture SHALL NOT be silently localized into one future HDIP plane without explicit justification that preserves its cross-cutting obligations.

name: Foundation separation
canonicalCondition: Compute, storage, networking, messaging, identity infrastructure, orchestration and other utility capabilities SHALL NOT acquire semantic, Product, governance or domain authority merely because they enable those responsibilities.

name: Architecture traceability
canonicalCondition: Every future canonical HDIP Plane, Overlay, ABB and material interaction SHALL trace to upstream responsibilities, explicit enterprise platform requirements and/or justified HDIP-specific coordination responsibilities.

name: Domain distinction
family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
canonicalCondition: Data, Information and Intelligence SHALL remain distinguishable architectural/semantic concerns even where one platform capability co-realizes responsibilities from more than one domain.

name: No cross-domain inheritance
family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
canonicalCondition: A Data-specific, Information-specific or Intelligence-specific construct SHALL NOT automatically generalize to the other domains through shared implementation or naming similarity.

name: No automatic Productness
family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
canonicalCondition: Composition, generation, transformation, persistence, deployment, publication, registration, cataloguing, marketplace presence, API exposure, repeated use or consumption SHALL NOT by itself establish Product identity.

name: Product-family distinction
family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
canonicalCondition: Co-realization of Data Products, Information Products and AI Products SHALL NOT collapse them into one HDIP-local Product family or type.

name: Composition non-inheritance
family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
canonicalCondition: Using, depending on, containing, deriving from or invoking a Product/capability SHALL NOT by itself transfer its Product family, ontology type, ownership or authority to the dependent/composed result.

name: Direct capability validity
family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
canonicalCondition: HDIP SHALL be able to support governed Data, Information or Intelligence capability use where Product qualification is not intended; Productization SHALL NOT be a mandatory gateway for every governed interaction.

name: Governed self-service
canonicalCondition: Self-service SHALL operate inside applicable authority, policy, security, privacy, quality, evidence and lifecycle constraints; self-service SHALL NOT mean unrestricted infrastructure or data access.

name: Intent/compilation separation
canonicalCondition: Participant-declared intent, business semantics and accountable judgement SHALL remain distinguishable from platform resolution, compilation, provisioning and automation.

name: Automation non-ownership
canonicalCondition: HDIP automation SHALL NOT transfer Product ownership, Data authority, policy authority or decision accountability to the compiler/runtime merely because the platform performs most technical work.

name: Judgement honesty
canonicalCondition: Architecture/governance decisions requiring contextual or accountable judgement SHALL NOT be represented as machine-proven solely because metadata, telemetry, rules or model outputs exist.

name: PDEP canonical lifecycle identity
canonicalCondition: PDEP SHALL remain the canonical HDIP Product Development and Evolution Process identity; historical SSPD terminology MAY remain only for traceability and SHALL NOT become a competing lifecycle.

name: Progressive PDEP projection
canonicalCondition: PDEP G0 and PDEP Spec A MAY compress/group canonical stages for progressive disclosure, while PDEP Spec C SHALL remain synchronized with the canonical applicable detailed PDEP lifecycle.

name: Experience non-authority
canonicalCondition: Interactive flow players, diagrams, dashboards and experience projections SHALL NOT independently create lifecycle stages, authority, Product identity, ABBs or architecture semantics.

name: Projection non-authority
canonicalCondition: HPD, SYNCTX, resolved graphs, compiled governance bundles, compilation packs and similar HDIP-generated projections SHALL NOT override the authoritative semantics or governance sources they reference.

name: Compiler non-invention
canonicalCondition: HDIP resolution/compilation SHALL NOT manufacture semantic relationships, Product identity, policy authority, joinability, provenance, dependencies or obligations from weak evidence or naming similarity.

name: Logical registry independence
canonicalCondition: ADS, Product, Schema, Policy, Capability and Blueprint registry responsibilities SHALL remain logically distinguishable even where one implementation realizes several of them.

name: Registry non-qualification
canonicalCondition: Registration SHALL NOT by itself prove authoritative status, Product status, control effectiveness, semantic correctness, fitness or HDIP conformance.

name: Registry/catalog/marketplace distinction
canonicalCondition: Registry, Catalog and Marketplace responsibilities SHALL NOT be treated as architectural synonyms even when exposed through one user experience or implementation.

name: Shared registry realization allowed
canonicalCondition: HDIP MAY consolidate registry implementation where operationally useful provided logical identities, ownership, contracts, lifecycle and authority boundaries remain distinguishable.

name: Evidence by construction
family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
canonicalCondition: Material HDIP interactions SHOULD emit or retain applicable provenance, control, quality, observability and lifecycle evidence sufficient for later reconstruction and assessment.

name: Trust is contextual
family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
canonicalCondition: Platform location, certification label, popularity, centralization, Product status or registry presence SHALL NOT be treated as universal proof of trust or fitness; trust assessment SHALL remain contextual and evidence-based.

name: Missing evidence is not positive evidence
family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
canonicalCondition: Missing, stale, inaccessible or materially ambiguous evidence SHALL NOT be interpreted as positive assurance.

name: Version/currentness distinction
family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
canonicalCondition: Version identity, latest/newest status and governed currentness SHALL remain distinguishable; newest SHALL NOT automatically mean current or approved.

name: Historical truth
family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
canonicalCondition: Later supersession, revocation, re-evaluation, upstream change, rollback or re-publication SHALL NOT silently rewrite which semantics, Product Version, policy/control, dependency, context or realization governed a historical occurrence.

name: Provenance is not assurance
family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
canonicalCondition: Provenance and lineage SHALL support traceability but SHALL NOT by themselves prove correctness, authorization, control effectiveness, assurance or Fitness for Use.

name: Canonical structure integrity
canonicalCondition: A conformant HDIP architecture SHALL preserve the canonical identity and responsibility meaning of P1-P5, X1-X9, HDIP-FND and the M08 ABB catalogue; implementation grouping, view projection or profile specialization SHALL NOT silently redefine those canonical structures.

name: Interaction-contract preservation
canonicalCondition: Material interactions SHALL preserve the applicable M12 Interaction Contract identity and obligations even when the participating responsibilities are co-located, embedded, distributed, provider-operated or implemented through a mechanism other than a network API.

name: External-boundary jurisdiction preservation
canonicalCondition: Material crossings of an M13 Boundary Family SHALL preserve the applicable external authority, jurisdiction, currentness, evidence and failure obligations; physical co-location or shared-provider realization SHALL NOT erase the logical boundary.

name: Product-access / consequence separation
canonicalCondition: Product or Product-Port access approval, entitlement or successful consumption SHALL NOT by itself authorize a downstream consequential Decision, Tool use, Digital Action or Physical Action where separate point-of-use authority is applicable.

name: Lifecycle / runtime non-equivalence
canonicalCondition: PDEP, SSCF and CEP SHALL remain lifecycle/experience compositions and SHALL NOT be interpreted as mandatory synchronous runtime pipelines; an established governed runtime MAY reuse current lifecycle state until material change requires re-evaluation.

name: Realization mapping traceability
canonicalCondition: A concrete realization claiming HDIP alignment SHALL retain traceability from applicable canonical responsibilities, ABBs, Interaction Contracts, Boundary Families and Profile obligations to the Realization Units, human processes or adjacent systems that satisfy them.

name: Adjacent-conformance independence
canonicalCondition: HDIP conformance SHALL NOT by itself establish conformance to GEDRA, GEARA, GEAIRA, BPS/PIN, a Product-family specification, an external standard or provider certification, and conformance to an adjacent specification SHALL NOT by itself establish HDIP conformance.

name: Profile monotonicity
canonicalCondition: An HDIP Profile MAY select, tighten, contextualize, specialize, narrow and extend the baseline for a bounded scope, but SHALL NOT weaken, waive or incompatibly redefine an applicable core invariant or transfer authority from an external semantic, Product, policy or Decision authority.
